result: The authors report that k-fibers in HeLa metaphase cells contain approximately 9 KMTs per kinetochore (8.5 ± 2.2, mean ±STD, n=292), based on electron tomography reconstructions of three complete spindles.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praised this work as 'an incredible resource for cell biologists' and noted the 'sophisticated reconstructions.' While reviewers requested additional EM images to support conclusions and raised methodological concerns about section collapse and MT tracking errors, they did not challenge the core KMT number finding itself. The data was accepted after corrections were made.

result: The authors claim that only about half (49% ±15.5%) of KMT minus ends reach the spindle pole (defined as within 1.7 µm MT-centrosome interaction area), with the average number of KMTs per k-fiber at the pole (4.1 ± 2.0) being lower than at the kinetochore (8.5 ± 2.2), suggesting a semi-direct connection model.
evaluation: Reviewers raised significant concerns about this interpretation. Reviewer 1 noted that 'the fact that so many KMTs do actually reach the pole is important and surprising to me' and questioned the arbitrary nature of the 1.7 µm cutoff definition. Reviewer 3 questioned whether the 40% of minus ends away from poles reflects 'poor MT tracking' and requested error analysis. Reviewers also noted that previous EM studies already showed semi-direct connections in mammalian spindles, questioning the novelty of this claim.

result: K-fibers show variation in circumference and KMT density along their length, with broadening at the pole-proximal side: the polygonal area is ~3-4 fold higher at poles compared to kinetochores, and only 64% of KMTs remain enclosed in the k-fiber circle at poles versus nearly 100% at kinetochores.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this finding but requested better motivation and clearer explanation. Reviewer 2 noted 'the polygon area analysis shown in Figure 6–supplement 1D is unclear and difficult to follow' and 'they did not address our comment that the polygon area analysis is never motivated or explained.' Despite requests for clarification, the core observation of k-fiber broadening was not disputed.

result: KMT associations with other MTs (both KMTs and non-KMTs) occur predominantly at spindle poles: 60.7 ± 9.4% of KMT minus-end associations with MT lattices and 59.8 ± 6.7% of KMT lattice associations with other MT minus ends were observed at poles (for 35 nm interaction distance).
evaluation: Reviewers raised major concerns about this conclusion. Reviewer 1 extensively critiqued that 'the preference for KMTs to have non-KMTs as neighbors near the pole...is uncorrected for two structural issues: the increased density of MTs near the poles...and the fact that there are many more non-KMT in this region.' Reviewer 1 insisted on normalization for MT density before making claims about preferential interactions. Reviewer 3 similarly noted 'the increased MT associations towards the pole can reflect simply this increased MT density.' The authors were required to normalize the data, which changed the interpretation.

result: KMTs display variable tortuosity (average 1.1 ± 0.1) that correlates with length (R=0.68) and position: straight KMTs (<1.1 tortuosity) are predominantly central while curved KMTs (>1.1) are peripheral, and local tortuosity increases from kinetochores toward poles (R=-0.13).
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the tortuosity measurements but requested better motivation. Reviewer 2 stated 'A different motivation is needed for the tortuosity analysis. Tortuosity reports on microtubule curvature, but NOT twist–it doesn't tell us anything about 3D helicity.' Reviewer 1 suggested the title 'K-fibers are broadened at spindle poles' was 'a bit of an exaggeration' and preferred 'widening' over 'splaying.' Despite these concerns about framing, the quantitative tortuosity data itself was not challenged.

result: Each HeLa metaphase spindle contains approximately 6300 MTs (6278 ± 1614) with pole-to-pole distance of 9.0 ± 1.7 µm, including 90-110 k-fibers with 859 ± 218 KMTs total, representing only ~14% of all MTs.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about the spindle length measurement. Reviewer 2 noted 'HeLa spindle lengths were previously reported to be ~12 µm, however, here they are reported to be significantly shorter in all spindles analyzed. The authors should clarify the origin of this discrepancy.' This suggests potential systematic measurement issues. Reviewer 1 also requested the discrepancy between 14% MT number versus 24% tubulin mass be explained, which was addressed by noting KMTs are longer on average.

result: The number of KMT attachments per kinetochore in metaphase is independent of both inter-kinetochore distance (Pearson's R=0.04-0.29) and k-fiber position within the spindle (central vs. intermediate vs. peripheral).
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these negative correlation findings. Reviewer 2 requested clarification of 'the motivation for comparing inter-kinetochore distance and the number of MTs at the kinetochore, and what previous evidence might suggest a correlation,' but the statistical analysis itself was accepted.

result: KMTs have an average length of 3.87 ± 1.98 µm with broad distribution (20% <2 µm, 39% >half-spindle length), while non-KMTs are shorter (2.0 ± 1.7 µm average) with exponential distribution favoring very short MTs.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these length measurements and noted they confirm previous observations. Reviewer 1 stated the data is 'in good agreement with Cherry's observations' and that length distributions are 'strikingly similar to the distribution obtained by biophysical modeling in combination with light microscopy.' Reviewer 3 requested analysis of whether MT ends could be generated by breaking, but did not challenge the length measurements themselves.

result: At 35 nm MT-MT distance, each KMT associates with 10.6 ± 3.2 other MTs with average association length of 145 ± 186 nm, while non-KMTs associate with 7.4 ± 3.1 other MTs with 103 ± 118 nm average length; KMTs show higher association numbers and lengths at increasing distances.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these quantitative measurements but requested clarification. Reviewer 1 noted 'you state that the number of associations was 10.6, but it is not clear what this number means. Number/KMT, per k-fiber or what?' The measurements themselves were not disputed, only their presentation needed improvement.

result: K-fibers in HeLa cells mediate a semi-direct connection with spindle poles where at least one KMT directly reaches the pole while others are indirectly linked to non-KMTs, similar to the anchoring pattern observed in C. elegans spindles.
evaluation: Reviewers challenged the novelty and framing of this conclusion. Reviewer 2 stated 'Previous EM studies in mammalian spindles have already shown that k-fibers form semi-direct connections to the pole' and suggested authors 'provide more context as to why their main point about a semi-direct connection between kinetochores and poles in human cells is novel and exciting.' Reviewer 1 noted the 'textbook models proposed and challenged in the text are not representative of the common understanding in the state of the field.'

result: The KMT length distribution in HeLa cells is strikingly similar to biophysical modeling predictions and to C. elegans embryos; KMTs are twice as long as non-KMTs on average, and the data supports a model where KMTs predominantly nucleate at kinetochores and grow toward poles.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these comparative analyses and integration with the parallel Conway et al. study. Reviewer 1 noted 'the addition of https://cfci.shinyapps.io/ASGA_3DViewer/ as a viewer tool is a major step in data sharing' and that the paper 'is now an excellent contribution to the literature.' However, Reviewer 1 cautioned that 'the statement that these and related data show that KMTs nucleate predominantly at kinetochores is true only for metaphase cells, and this limitation must be stated.'

result: KMTs display open flared ends at kinetochores; the average kinetochore area is 0.10 ± 0.07 µm² with KMT density of 112 ± 60 KMTs/µm² and center-to-center spacing of 74 ± 22 nm (corresponding to ~50 nm wall-to-wall spacing).
evaluation: Reviewers questioned the kinetochore size measurements. Reviewer 1 noted 'you estimated the size of each kinetochore by the area occupied by the KMTs...you then go on to calculate the correlation between the number of KMTs and the size of the area they occupy and get a great correlation. But this is not meaningful. Of course, you get a good correlation because you are estimating the size of the kinetochore by the area occupied by the MTs.' This circular reasoning undermines confidence in the kinetochore area measurements.

result: The difference in KMT number between HeLa cells (~9 KMTs) and PtK1 cells (~20 KMTs) correlates with kinetochore size differences (HeLa: 0.107 ± 0.075 µm² vs. PtK1: 0.157 ± 0.045 µm²), suggesting kinetochore area may define available MT binding sites.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this comparative analysis and interpretation. The discussion contextualizes the findings within previous literature on different cell types. No specific concerns were raised about this comparison, though the kinetochore size measurement method was questioned elsewhere.

result: Central KMTs are shorter with minus ends closer to the mother centriole compared to peripheral KMTs, likely related to the roundedness of mitotic spindles, suggesting k-fiber position affects individual KMT ultrastructure.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this positional analysis. Reviewer 2 requested the authors 'explain the significance of finding more KMT minus-ends at spindle poles in central k-fibers compared to peripheral k-fibers' and 'consider plotting KMT length versus kinetochore region,' which was addressed. The finding itself was not disputed.
